notes: Published L., D., VI, Bl. 4, no. 13; photo Berlin Academy. Griffith translates 'The honoured(?) strategus of the water, sate of Bekemete, Manitawawi; yetetake of the wete in Shiye(?) and chief wemañas in Philae, prophet of the king(?), royal consort(?) of (the king's) mother(?), khabkhañ and chief shaqate, malêshatêkhe'; the same man is labelled in 105. His '?' stands over the first sign of Siyeteli. Words are spaced as printed (word gaps measured): qorito is one word (the 2026-11-09 test split it), qo(15)re and yetet(10)ke are single words cut by the line number. Re-read from the type for the codes; the test's m in womñt- is ẖ, as the test itself found. FHN III no. 267 differs at womnetẖ, sqotelẖlo and mlostoselo (Griffith renders shaqate and malêshatêkhe, backing the type). [Signs read: 103; marked '?': 1 (1 carry Griffith's printed '?', 0 are my doubts)]. '(n)' in text_std is Griffith's superscript stone-line number.

His note (p. 39): after nobow (nêbêw, 'gold (?)') there seem to be numerals (cf. 101/8), and the last word is kelbo or klebo, its o made vertical between the outlines of the staff; the type runs × and an n-shaped sign on to kelbo with no space, written here {×}{numeral like n} (dropped from text_corpus); FHN III no. 267 reads '35 kelbo'. His '?' stands over the b and l of kelbo. The type has m in mte where FHN reads ste. 'a (5)tolit' and 'mni(10)se' are spaced as printed (FHN atolit, Mnise). Same signs as the 2026-11-09 test, except that × n is taken as numerals following Griffith. [Signs read: 71; marked '?': 2 (2 carry Griffith's printed '?', 0 are my doubts)]. notes: Published L., D., VI, Bl. 2, no. 7; photo no. 720. All 7 '?' are Griffith's. His notes: l. 1 'The honourable Mashtaraq'; l. 2 bedewi is perhaps the place-name Bezewe (see 89); p?Sdk is 'altered to or from' a form with m (or h) as first sign; l. 3 wiyleb is a plural; l. 4 ptl?teb is 'a genitive plural adjective, (things) of patal (?)'; l. 5 ptrq, cf. the name Mashtirq; the last group recurs elsewhere, 'but the ob looks more like r, an improbable initial'. Its third sign has the pointed h-form (X), checked at 2.5x against the m of mStrq and the X of XeN; FHN III reads m. Against the test's readings.md: type lines 1 and 2 agree (its '[e?]' in dxe is Griffith's printed '?'); type line 3 (stone ll. 4-6), which the test's crop missed, is new here. [Signs read: 60; marked '?': 7 (7 carry Griffith's printed '?', 0 are my doubts)]. '(n)' in text_std is Griffith's superscript stone-line number.
